title: Project skills & tools — the remaining sign-offs

steps.headline: Build the controls for ordinary projects first, and add Your Assistant's locked switches once that project exists?
steps.today: Every skill and tool connection you install is on in every project. The planned built-in Your Assistant project does not exist in the app yet; it is separate work scheduled for release 1.3.1.
steps.problem: Your decisions say the four built-in plugins are always on and locked in Your Assistant. Building that part now would mean waiting for Your Assistant, or faking it.
steps.proposal: Ship per-project switches for ordinary projects first. When Your Assistant is built, its locked, dimmed built-in switches (already mocked) are added then. You approved this in chat; this records it.

options.label: Ordinary projects first
pros: You get project controls without waiting on unrelated work
The locked-switch design is kept, just added later
cons: Until Your Assistant exists, the built-in plugins can be switched off in any project — only by your choice

options.label: Wait for Your Assistant
cons: This feature waits on a separate project with no firm date

steps.headline: If you change a project's switches while a conversation is open, which status should that conversation's skill chips show?
steps.today: The drawer mockup shows green Automatic, amber Manual use and red Unavailable chips. Your decision says switch changes only affect NEW conversations.
steps.problem: An already-open conversation keeps what it started with. If its chips showed the new setting, a green Automatic chip could appear on a skill the assistant in that conversation cannot actually see.
steps.proposal: The chips show what THIS conversation has. When the project's setting differs, the drawer adds one quiet line: 'Project settings changed — they apply in your next new conversation.'

options.label: What this conversation has
pros: Chips always tell the truth about what the assistant can use right now
The note explains why a switch you just flipped hasn't taken effect
cons: Right after changing a switch, the chips don't match the Projects screen until you start a new conversation

options.label: The new setting
pros: Chips always match the Projects screen
cons: Chips can say Automatic for a skill the assistant can't see in this conversation, which is misleading

steps.surface: Projects → Skills & tools → Needs setup on this device
steps.path: Projects → a synced project → Skills & tools → Set up here
steps.headline: For something turned on in a project but missing on this device, what should 'Set up here' offer in the first version?
steps.today: Nothing in the app lets you set up a tool connection (MCP server) by hand, and personal skill files don't sync between devices yet.
steps.problem: A project synced from another device can have a skill or tool connection turned on that isn't installed here. The button needs a real next step, not a promise it can't keep.
steps.proposal: The button opens a short explanation of why it's missing, plus 'Ask assistant to set it up' (starts a conversation that walks you through it) and, for a skill, 'Choose skill file'. Shown on the setup slides below.

options.label: Assistant plus file picker
pros: Works for every kind of missing item on day one
Picking a file is quick when you already have the skill file
cons: Setting up a tool connection goes through a conversation rather than a form

options.label: Assistant only
pros: One clear button, smallest to build
cons: No quick path when you already have the skill file

options.label: A real setup screen
pros: A form for tool connections, no conversation needed
cons: A whole new screen to design and review first, which delays the feature

steps.path: Android app → Projects → a project → Skills & tools
steps.headline: Conversations started on your phone run through Claude Code, which these switches can't control yet. What should the phone show?
steps.today: On Android, conversations run through Claude Code rather than YouCoded's own assistant. Your decision keeps Claude Code untouched unless you opt in later.
steps.problem: If the phone shows the same switches with no note, flipping one appears to do something but changes nothing for conversations started on the phone.
steps.proposal: Show the tab on Android so the project's choices are visible and editable, with one line: 'These apply to conversations on your computer. Phone conversations aren't affected yet.'

options.label: Show, with a note
pros: You can still manage a synced project's choices from your phone
Honest about what the switches do there
cons: One more line of text on the phone

options.label: Hide on Android
pros: Nothing on the phone that doesn't apply there
cons: You can't change a project's choices from your phone at all

steps.headline: Are the chips in the right place now?
steps.changed: Each status chip sits at the right edge of its skill card. The red Unavailable chip no longer has a separate 'Set up in Projects' caption, and the chip colors come from the same source as the session switcher's.
steps.notice: Clicking the red chip, or anywhere on its dimmed card, opens that project's setup rows. Hover brightens it; the missing skill still can't run.
steps.risk: The statuses are sample data; nothing real is decided by them yet.

steps.headline: After Install finishes, should this panel turn into 'choose your projects'?
steps.changed: A new download starts off in every project. The same panel switches to a project list: open a project, turn Inbox on, and choose its skills. Do as many projects as you like.
steps.notice: Done or closing keeps the download installed even if nothing was turned on; you can finish later in Projects. Choices now stay put if you close and reopen during the preview, and show up in that project's Skills & tools tab.
steps.risk: Sample projects and a fake install; nothing is saved to disk yet.

steps.headline: Do the project list, switches and Done button fit on your phone?
steps.changed: The same panel on a phone: the first project opens so the plugin and its skill are visible without another tap, and the list scrolls if it grows.
steps.notice: Each project opens separately. The plugin's main switch pauses automatic use but remembers which skills you picked.
steps.risk: Preview only; no project settings are saved yet.

steps.surface: Projects → Skills & tools on a phone
steps.path: Projects → a project → Skills & tools → scroll to the bottom
steps.headline: On a phone, the instructions under each row now wrap instead of being cut off. Keep it?
steps.changed: Row descriptions wrap onto a second line on narrow screens. The last round cut 'Add the skill file here…' off mid-word. Both buttons now read 'Set up here'.
steps.notice: Rows are a little taller on phones; on a computer nothing changes because the text already fits.
steps.risk: A very long plugin name could make a row three lines tall.

steps.surface: Projects → Skills & tools on a phone
steps.path: Projects → a synced project → Skills & tools → Set up here
steps.headline: Does 'Set up here' explain what's missing and offer a real next step?
steps.changed: The button used to do nothing. It now opens a short box saying why the item is missing on this device, with 'Ask assistant to set it up' (and 'Choose skill file' for a personal skill).
steps.notice: Pressing the button again closes the box. Which buttons ship is the question on the earlier page; this shows the recommended option.
steps.risk: The buttons inside the box do nothing in this preview.

steps.path: Projects → a project → Skills & tools → turn on Research Kit
steps.headline: Is this the right warning before turning on a plugin that connects to outside services?
steps.changed: Turning on a plugin with a tool connection shows one confirmation that names every part that can connect or run by itself. The plugin stays off unless you press Enable.
steps.notice: It appears every time you turn such a part on, as you decided. Plugins with only skills turn on with no warning.
steps.risk: The wording is new and hasn't been shown to you before.
